h:
You can configure most game and place-level settings from the Creator Dashboard, a hub that lets you manage and access all of your Roblox creations in one place. It's useful to explore the left-hand navigation to see every configuration possible, such as those for localization, analytics, and monetization, but the following sections highlight notable workflows for most games.

Generate content descriptors

The Maturity & Compliance Questionnaire contains a set of questions about the type of content players can possibly encounter within your game, as well as how frequently it occurs. Your answers give Roblox an understanding of the content in your game and ensure that the game is available to the appropriate audience on the Home and Discover pages according to each player's age group and regional content policies.

For step-by-step instructions on how to fill out the questionnaire, see content maturity & compliance.

Set age and geography restrictions

You can set restrictions so that only players over a certain age or from specific regions can play and discover your games. This is particularly helpful when you want to age up your audience without including mature content to age gate through content maturity labels.

To set age and geography restrictions:

  1. Navigate to the Creator Dashboard.
  2. Click on the thumbnail of the game for which you want to set age and geography restrictions. The game's Overview page displays.
  3. In the left-hand navigation, navigate to Audience ⟩ Access Settings.
  4. In the Age section, set Minimum age to the youngest age a player can have to access your game.
  5. In the Region section, enable every region that can access your game.
  6. At the bottom of the page, click the Save Changes button.

Copy landing page link

After you publish your game, Roblox generates a landing page for the game referred to as the game's main details page. You can access and copy this link from either the Creator Dashboard or the Roblox app, then share it with others so they can play your game.

  1. Hover over a game's thumbnail, click the ⋯ button, and select Copy URL.

  1. Share the copied URL with others as a direct link to the game's landing page featuring a play button.

  1. Open the Roblox app on your mobile device.
  2. Locate the game, typically under the Continue header on the home screen, and tap its tile to open the info screen.
  3. In the lower-left corner of the screen, click the ⋯ button and select Share to open your device's sharing options.

Edit collaborator permissions

When creating and collaborating on games as part of a group, abilities granted to group members are dependent on their role permissions. Owners or other group members with sufficient permissions can adjust play/edit/publish access and more on a per‑game level, such as allowing a limited group role the ability to edit a specific game even if that role cannot edit all games.

For step-by-step instructions on how to edit collaborator permissions, see roles and permissions.

Access version history

Roblox automatically retains saved versions of each place for version control and backup purposes. You can access Version History in the Creator Dashboard to revert to a previously saved version of any place within a game, or in Studio to leave notes attached to your saved place files.

For more information about accessing Version History, saving place files with notes, and reverting to previous place versions, see Version History.

Allow copying

By default, all games are locked so that you or your group are the only creators who have permission to edit its place files. However, if you want to allow other creators to be able to access an editable copy of your game for their own creation process, you can uncopylock the game. This is particularly helpful when you create templates or reference files for open use.

To allow the community to access an editable copy of your game:

  1. Navigate to the Creator Dashboard.
  2. Click on the thumbnail of the game you want to allow players to copy. The game's Overview page displays.
  3. In the left-hand navigation, navigate to Configurations ⟩ Places.
  4. Click the start place marked with a star icon. The place's Basic Settings page displays.

  1. In the place's left-hand navigation menu, select Permissions.
  2. Enable Allow users to download a copy of this Place.
  3. Click the Save Changes button. Your game is now uncopylocked and creators can access an editable copy of it from the game's main page by clicking the ⋯ button and selecting Edit in Studio.

Allow strong language

You can enable strong language and relax the text chat filter in your games for older player audiences. Doing so also adds a tag above your game page to warn other players that your game may include strong language:

Regardless of whether or not you activate the toggle, players do not face moderation consequences just for using strong language in chat or voice in games with Restricted content maturity labels, but they cannot violate Community Standards and Terms of Use. For example, players can type an expletive if they are scared by a monster, but they cannot abuse another player using strong language or otherwise.

In-game assets and game metadata cannot contain strong language, even if the toggle is on and your game has a Restricted content maturity label. If you include strong language in your assets or game page, your game will be moderated.

To allow strong language between players in text chat within your game:

  1. Navigate to the Creator Dashboard and click on the thumbnail of the game in which you want to allow strong language. The game's Overview page displays.
  2. In the left-hand navigation, navigate to Audience ⟩ Communication Settings.
  3. Enable the Allow Strong Language toggle, then press the Save Changes button. Players within your game can now use strong language in text chat.

kid.simple: After you publish a game, you change most of its settings on the Creator Dashboard, a website page where all your creations live. This page walks through the most useful settings: telling Roblox what content is in your game, limiting who can play by age or country, sharing a link to your game, giving teammates access, going back to older versions, letting others copy your game, and allowing strong language for older players. These settings decide who sees your game and how safe it is, so they matter as much as the game itself.
kid.analogy: The Creator Dashboard is like the settings menu on a phone. The phone (your game) works without touching it, but that menu is where you decide who can call you, which apps can see your photos, and what language it speaks.
keyPoints: Fill out the Maturity & Compliance Questionnaire so Roblox knows what content is in your game and shows it to the right ages on the Home and Discover pages.
Under Audience > Access Settings you can set a minimum age and choose which regions can play, then click Save Changes.
To share your game, hover its thumbnail on the Creator Dashboard, click the three-dot button, and pick Copy URL. On the Roblox app, use the three-dot button and Share.
In a group, what each member can do depends on their role, but owners can give extra access to one specific game.
Roblox saves versions of every place automatically, and Version History lets you go back to an older one.
Games are copylocked by default. To let others download an editable copy, open the start place's Permissions and turn on Allow users to download a copy of this Place.

Allow Strong Language (under Audience > Communication Settings) relaxes the chat filter for older players and adds a warning tag to your game page. Your own assets, name, and description still cannot contain strong language.

terms.Creator Dashboard: The Roblox website page at create.roblox.com where you manage your games and their settings.
terms.content descriptors: Short labels that describe what is in your game, such as mild violence. They come from your answers to the questionnaire.
terms.age gate: A rule that blocks players below a certain age from joining.
terms.region: A country or area of the world. You can choose which ones can play your game.
terms.landing page: Your game's main page on Roblox with the big Play button. Also called the main details page.
terms.collaborator: Another person who helps build your game, like a teammate in your group.
terms.role permissions: The list of things a group role is allowed to do, such as edit or publish games.
terms.version control: Keeping old saved copies so you can compare or go back if something breaks.
terms.revert: Go back to an older saved version.
terms.copylocked: Locked so nobody except you or your group can get an editable copy of the place. This is the default.
terms.uncopylock: Unlock a game so anyone can open an editable copy of it in Studio. Useful for templates you want to share.
terms.strong language: Swear words and rude words. The setting is meant for older audiences only.

watchOut: Uncopylocking a game you care about. Anyone can then get an editable copy of your whole place, scripts included. Only do it for templates you want to share.

Thinking Allow Strong Language lets you put swear words in your game's name, description, or signs. It only affects player chat, and your game can be moderated for strong language in its assets or page.
Forgetting to click Save Changes at the bottom of a settings page. Your changes are not kept until you do.
